correctness.rationale: In a natural basis the form B is diagonal with both entries nonzero by nondegeneracy. A basis up to separately rescaling and reordering is an unordered pair of transverse orthogonal lines; orthogonal complementation on nonisotropic lines is a fixed-point-free involution. Rescaling u rescales B, changing its determinant by a square and leaving B(u,u)=0 invariant. An automorphism has Tu=cu and B(Tx,Ty)=cB(x,y). If B(u,u)≠0 then c=1 and T is ±1 on the orthogonal line while fixing u. If B(u,u)=0, choose an isotropic v with B(u,v)=1 by subtracting B(v,v)u/2 from a suitably normalized mate. The same equations force Tv=v, and all nonzero c are allowed. There are at most two exceptional isotropic lines over an infinite field, giving infinitude; dimension one has only one basis class under scaling. Over an odd finite field the isotropic line count is 1+χ(-Δ), giving N. In the hyperbolic coordinates L_t=K(u+tv), complementation sends t to -t and the automorphism sends t to t/c, proving transitivity. For nonisotropic u, the reflection fixes the coordinate pair. Any other fixed pair must be swapped; orthogonality of u+tv and u-tv requires t²=B(u,u)/B(v,v), and such lines are nonisotropic because their norm is 2B(u,u)≠0. Two roots give one pair exactly when χ(Δ)=1. Burnside gives the claimed O and the fixed-point count, including the small fields.
residual_risks: The package enumerates examples over prime fields, not all odd prime powers. The projective-line and character arguments establish the general count, including nonprime odd fields; the structure argument also applies in characteristic zero.

residual_risks: The frozen related-work discussion should credit the A5 K× case alongside A8,alpha; no novelty credit is given here for either group calculation or for N(E) independently.

value.rationale: The equivalence by scaling and reordering is the one singled out by the survey. Computing how many of those bases remain inequivalent after intrinsic symmetry answers a further natural classification question, which knowing the group and the total number of bases does not settle. For example, a hyperbolic form over F7 gives three basis classes for either generator type, while an isotropic generator leaves one automorphism orbit and a nonisotropic one leaves two. The count distinguishes a concrete effect of the distinguished derived line, rather than tabulating illustrative prime-field examples.
residual_risks: This is a classification of naturally marked decompositions up to the stated equivalences in dimension two, not an all-dimensional or characteristic-two moduli theorem.
